notes: Fifth sweep (2026-10-22-d, result.json head ba24972): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0 and a model_id matching the requested model; reads is empty in all five, and each transcript shows a single Write call, no Skill, Read or Bash call.

None of the nine listed rules changed since 3e3581d: `git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/` touches SKILL.md (the reference table's test trigger, a new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, the text of "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call", the do: rule, Before you finish step 1) and renames testing.md to ex_unit.md with a reworded Assert with patterns. `git diff ba24972 HEAD -- idiomatic-elixir/` is empty, so the runs saw the current text. All nine are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/library-client-baseline.json: an option value passed to Req unchecked (and an API key checked only for nil or truthiness) violates Make polymorphism explicit; ## Options in the @moduledoc instead of new/1's @doc counts against Group related parameters; an API key held in a Req request inside a package struct with no Inspect handling is violated, and a key never stored in a package struct is not exercised; a public @doc false function without @spec violates Add specs, and message/1 under @impl needs none.

Two judgement calls under that standard. Keep secrets: opus-1 hides the key with a hand-written `defimpl Inspect` (lines 37-41) instead of `@derive`, which meets the rule's aim, so it is clean. sonnet-1 returns the bare Req request as its client (`@type t :: Req.Request.t()`, line 31); no struct the package defines holds the key, so the verdict is not exercised, but the case's inspect check is marked missed because that value still prints the header. Use exception structs: haiku-1's WeatherClient.Error is a plain defstruct (line 124), so it is violated even though the reason is a struct.

Tier results that differ from the 2026-10-22-c baseline sweep come from the runs, not the rules. Take configuration as arguments is now violated for Sonnet (both runs fall back to Application.get_env in new/1; clean last sweep). Keep secrets is clean for Opus (the custom Inspect implementation; violated last sweep). Add specs is clean for Haiku (haiku-1 specs its @doc false helpers, haiku-2 has none; violated last sweep).

Changed rules outside the list, applied to other_violations under their current text. "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" is now decided by "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal" and "A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline": opus-1's `opts = Keyword.validate!(opts, [` (lines 61-67) and haiku-2's `req = Req.new(` (lines 55-60), shapes the previous sweep counted against the rule, are bound to a name and now pass; every other multi-line keyword list is built under a name first (haiku-1 req_opts, line 49) or heads a pipeline as a literal (opus-1 line 79, sonnet-1 line 54, sonnet-2 line 95), which the pipeline rule allows. The do: rule now allows a function to mix forms ("A function may mix the forms"); no run wraps a do: body onto its own line. The new Formatting bullet and Before you finish step 1 apply to sessions that could run shell commands; every file passes mix format --check-formatted, so neither is broken. Other other_violations follow the previous standard (a status range that contradicts the error docs) plus two shapes not seen before in this case: required response fields read with map["key"] (sonnet-1, sonnet-2) and an unused head binding that warns at compile (haiku-1), and one iex> example that cannot run as a doctest (haiku-1).
format_ok in result.json was confirmed with mix format --check-formatted on copies in the scratch folder: all five files pass. No session ran mix format or a compile.

Compile results come from result.json and are not graded. opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 compile, with warnings only for the absent Req (and Jason in haiku-2). haiku-1 and sonnet-1 do not compile for a reason unrelated to Req: WeatherClient builds %Error{} (haiku-1 line 41, sonnet-1 line 75) before the file defines WeatherClient.Error. Compiled with the modules reordered in the scratch folder, sonnet-1 warns only about Req, and haiku-1 also warns that `body` is unused at line 98.
Expected reads (library-design.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline.
